rows.note: For an everyday ironic remark, this is the all-purpose choice.

example.english: He says he hates being late, but he is always late—that's pure irony.
example.traditional: 佢話自己最憎遲到，點知成日都遲到，真係反話喎。
example.jyutping: keoi5 waa6 zi6 gei2 zeoi3 zang1 ci4 dou3 dim2 zi1 seng4 jat6 dou1 ci4 dou3 zan1 hai6 faan2 waa2 wo3

rows.note: Use this for the ironic quality or significance of a situation rather than an individual remark.

example.english: He took every safety precaution, yet ended up falling at home; the situation is full of irony.
example.traditional: 佢做足安全措施，最後反而喺屋企跌親，件事好有諷刺意味。
example.jyutping: keoi5 zou6 zuk1 on1 cyun4 cou3 si1 zeoi3 hau6 faan2 ji4 hai2 uk1 kei2 dit3 can1 gin6 si6 hou2 jau5 fung3 ci3 ji3 mei6

rows.note: Use this technical term when the audience understands the significance of a situation but the characters do not.

example.english: Onstage, the audience knows the killer is behind the door, but the heroine walks over anyway; the dramatic irony is very strong.
example.traditional: 舞台上，觀眾知道兇手就喺門後，但女主角仲行埋去，呢種戲劇反諷好強。
